articles.title: Injury Report: Thorpe and Mr. Clanky face long absences
articles.dek: Mt. Silver and Lavender prepare new passing plans; Mahogany loses Watchog; the full league recovery comparison.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Two winning teams lose important passers

Mt. Silver’s Tic Thorpe has a new six-week report after throwing for 244 yards and two touchdowns against Saffron. Josh Alakazam still has seven reported weeks remaining. Crem Ftzpatrik completed five of eight for 69 yards and a touchdown, then directed the winning field-goal drive. His actual relief work makes him a demonstrated option before Cinnabar; a future starting assignment still requires the team’s decision. Foo Warner has a new two-week report, and cornerback Ninjask has one.

Lavender’s Mr. Clanky has a new eight-week report. His listed position is SLOT, but he completed six of eight passes for 121 yards and a touchdown against Celadon. Frosmoth supplied 163 passing yards in the same win. The Wails must prepare the available passing group for Cerulean while People Eater remains out two weeks. The injury record does not identify either passer’s precise injury play.
New absences around the league

Mahogany’s outside linebacker Watchog has a new seventeen-week report, the largest new recovery duration this week. Jellicent is out two weeks, adding another receiving absence while Golduck continues his recovery. The Frost visit Vermilion, whose offense was shut out at Olivine. Their defensive replacements must preserve the opportunity created by that matchup.

Cinnabar’s Seismitoad has a new two-week report after four carries for 16 yards. Pidgeotto finished the Blackthorn win with useful late runs and totaled 25 yards on three attempts; he is one observed contributor for the staff to consider before Mt. Silver. Oreburgh’s fullback Swampert is newly out four weeks before Dewford. Cianwood receiver Doduo has one week, and Azalea safety Castform has two. These are reported durations rather than guaranteed return dates.
Recovery changes before the marquee matchup

Mossdeep’s Marshall Flock and Luvrelle Revis have cleared their previous positive recovery counters. Sunyshore’s FLOAT SZN has also cleared his. Those changes improve the availability picture before the Starseekers visit the Eclipse, but do not establish an appearance or starting role. Serp Gardener still has one reported week, Ninjaskamara one and Richard Furman two. Rustboro’s My Way, Son has three before Canalave.

The full table compares the current report with the previous issue, separating new injuries from ordinary countdown changes and cleared designations. Zero weeks means no remaining absence is reported; it does not establish game participation. Positions are the current listed positions. No diagnoses, unsupported doubtful labels or certain return dates are added.

articles.title: Game of the Week: Sunyshore brings a complete offense to Mossdeep’s bye test
articles.dek: The 11–3 Starseekers have a productive runner, four touchdown catches from 88 Special, and one remaining route to the first seed. Mossdeep can settle the race with a win or tie.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Sunyshore arrives at Mossdeep with a convincing answer to the simplest question about this matchup: can the Starseekers do enough on offense to make the Eclipse defend a complete game? They just ran for 175 yards, passed for 279 and scored forty-one against Rustboro. Myles Gabite supplied 144 rushing yards. DeZhaun Watzon threw four touchdown passes, all to 88 Special, while three other receivers also made substantial contributions. Karson Jones has several productive ways to begin the conversation.

The next question is harder. Can Sunyshore keep Dram Marino and Accel BeckhmJr from turning a good Starseekers possession into a brief interruption? Mossdeep has scored 185 points in its last three games. Marino threw seven touchdown passes against Petalburg, then seven more at Canalave. BeckhmJr followed five touchdown catches with four, including a sixty-one-yard score. An opponent can play respectable offense and still spend most of this game needing the ball back.

I pick Mossdeep 38, Sunyshore 21. The Starseekers have the balance to make the unbeaten team work, and their eleven victories deserve more consideration than a glance at the Eclipse's latest margin. I favor Mossdeep because its passing production has remained both spectacular and careful. Marino has fifty-four touchdown passes against three interceptions. Sunyshore still has Serp Gardener unavailable for one reported week, removing a coverage option just as the league's most productive passing combination comes into view.
The bye is available at Mossdeep's own stadium

Mossdeep is 14–0 and has already won Hoenn East. Sunyshore is 11–3 and has already won Sinnoh East. A Mossdeep win or tie secures the Hoenn–Sinnoh first seed and the opening-round bye. Sunyshore has to win to keep its route open, then continue winning at Pastoria and Veilstone while hoping Mossdeep loses its final two games against Sootopolis and Lavaridge. In that possible 14–3 tie, this head-to-head result would belong to the Starseekers.

That gives both coaches a specific reward to discuss. Michael Dorrill can give his players a week without an opening-round game by winning now. Jones can keep a difficult pursuit alive while proving his team can beat the conference leader on the road. Neither needs to invent a season-defining label for an ordinary fixture. The standings have already provided the stakes.

“We've earned the right to walk in there expecting to play well,” Jones said. “That expectation has to show up in the blocking, in the routes, in the way we finish the tackle. You want attention? Give people a reason to keep watching the next snap.” His team supplied those reasons against Rustboro after falling behind seven-zero. The forty-one unanswered points came from sustained productivity rather than a series of gifts: neither club lost a turnover.
Gabite gives Sunyshore a way to choose the next down

Gabite carried sixteen times for 144 yards and two touchdowns. His twenty-six-yard run up the middle tied the Rustboro game in the first quarter, and his three-yard fourth-down run supplied Sunyshore's final touchdown late in the fourth. The Starseekers could use him for an explosive answer and for the short finish of a longer possession. That combination made Watzon's passing work considerably easier to defend in theory than in practice.

The performance was also a substantial expansion of Gabite's season production. He now has 269 rushing yards on forty-two carries, meaning more than half those yards arrived against the Stone. I would treat that as a powerful recent observation and still ask him to repeat the useful parts. One afternoon does not establish that nine yards a carry is now Sunyshore's ordinary expectation.

Mossdeep gave Canalave ninety-three rushing yards on thirty-four attempts. Seismitoad accounted for eighty-one of them on twenty-two carries. That is a more restrained defensive result than the Bulwark's 334 total yards might suggest. Sunyshore will need its runs to create favorable passing situations, rather than simply demonstrating patience while the scoreboard moves against it.

My rushing target for the Starseekers is 120 yards. That would be below their Rustboro total but enough to give the passing game genuine assistance. It matters how those yards arrive: a useful first-down gain gives Watzon choices, while a late run against a large deficit may improve the total without helping the next scoring chance. I will also watch whether Sunyshore can avoid asking for repeated difficult third-down completions.
Four touchdown catches do not account for the whole passing game

88 Special caught six passes for seventy-seven yards and four touchdowns against Rustboro. The scores traveled ten, seventeen, twenty-five and eight yards, with two to each broad side of the field. Watzon did not need the same distance or the same side every time he looked for the receiver. Mossdeep has to defend the finishing route without allowing the other targets to move the possession into range.

Jolt Vick had six catches for eighty-seven yards. Fera LaGatr caught six for seventy-six. MF STOMP added four catches for thirty-four, and BAXXED? caught the remaining completion. Those twenty-three completed passes gave Sunyshore several productive destinations. Calling for more attention on 88 Special is an understandable opening instruction; the following instruction must explain who handles the other receivers.

Watzon finished twenty-three of thirty without an interception. That accuracy is particularly useful against a Mossdeep defense that recorded seven sacks against Petalburg and four at Canalave. Joey Sporeter had two sacks in the latter game and recovered Canalave's lost fumble. Sunyshore cannot assume that a covered first option will leave unlimited time to locate the second.

The Eclipse's practical target is to hold Sunyshore below forty percent on third down. Rustboro allowed three conversions in seven chances, but the Starseekers did enough work before third down that the offense never depended on a large volume of conversions. Mossdeep needs to make those late downs both more frequent and less manageable. That is a defensive task involving the run fits, coverage and rush together.
BeckhmJr makes an ordinary coverage error unusually expensive

BeckhmJr caught ten passes for 270 yards at Canalave. His four touchdowns included the sixty-one-yard throw deep left early in the second quarter, a twenty-nine-yard score deep right, a six-yard finish short left and a twenty-one-yard touchdown deep right. The variety matters. Sunyshore has to limit both the immediate explosive gain and the shorter completion that finishes a possession already moving successfully.

His season line is seventy-five catches, 1,875 yards and thirty-one receiving touchdowns. Marino has 4,025 passing yards. Those totals make a plan built entirely around waiting for a bad throw difficult to defend. Mossdeep's quarterback has thrown only three interceptions in 348 attempts, and Sunyshore did not force a giveaway against Rustboro. The visitors need successful coverage and pressure on ordinary plays as well as whatever exceptional opportunity appears.

Sunyshore should also account for Ninjulio Jones, who caught four passes for seventy-two yards and a touchdown at Canalave. Gronkaludon caught all three of his targets, including a touchdown. Shawn Mareman added a receiving score. An extra defender attending to BeckhmJr has to come from somewhere, and Marino has just demonstrated several ways to use the remaining space.

I want Mossdeep to allow no more than two sacks. That is a concrete protection standard against a defense that held Rustboro to five first downs and one third-down conversion in eleven attempts. The Eclipse allowed one sack in Canalave's box score and scored without punting. Sunyshore offers a more demanding test of how consistently that protection can preserve Marino's choices.
The injury reports improve in places without settling the lineup

Gardener's remaining absence is Sunyshore's clearest continuing concern. FLOAT SZN no longer has a reported week of absence, while Scol Alexander's new minor designation carries no remaining absence. Those updates improve the available information without establishing a starting assignment or the workload any player will receive.

Mossdeep's Marshall Flock and Luvrelle Revis likewise have no remaining reported absence. Ninjaskamara is still listed for one week and Richard Furman for two. Mareman and Poury Holt have handled useful backfield work during the absences, but the Eclipse's latest wins have been driven overwhelmingly by the passing game. Sunyshore's task is to force more possessions in which that passing advantage has to be earned over several snaps.

“We gave up a touchdown,” Dorrill said of the 51–7 win at Canalave. “That possession is in the review. So is the missed extra point. The next opponent doesn't owe us the same mistakes, and the score doesn't excuse ours.” Sunyshore's six-touchdown performance gives that insistence a practical setting. An eleven-win visitor can make small failures cost more than they did against an offense that reached the end zone once.

For Sunyshore to win, Gabite must help the offense remain balanced, Watzon must keep finding the productive receiver without giveaways, and the defense must hold Mossdeep to substantially fewer touchdown passes than its recent seven-per-game rate. My checkable ceiling for the visitors is four passing touchdowns allowed. They can then try to win a game in which their own offense reaches the thirties.

I expect Mossdeep's receivers to exceed the visitors' ability to trade scoring possessions for a full afternoon. Sunyshore can move the ball and score enough to demand attention, but Marino's season-long combination of production and ball security gives the Eclipse the stronger way to finish. Mossdeep 38, Sunyshore 21, with the first seed and bye secured at home.

articles.title: Seven berths secured, two byes available—and nine wild-card endings
articles.dek: Saffron and Cinnabar win divisions, Petalburg qualifies, and Mossdeep can settle its bye against Sunyshore. Ellis Quill follows the verified routes and the ties that change the field.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Cinnabar won a division by beating Blackthorn. Saffron won a division on the same afternoon it lost at Mt. Silver. Petalburg escaped Pastoria by one point and secured a playoff place. Three games remain, seven clubs have qualified, and the rewards still available range from a first-round bye to the simple relief of knowing there will be a nineteenth week.

I would allow each of those teams an evening to appreciate the achievement. Saffron has surrendered only 115 points in fourteen games; one painful 36–33 loss does not erase that season. Petalburg has ten victories despite being outscored overall. Cinnabar followed an 18–17 loss at Cerulean with a division-clinching win at Blackthorn. Their routes have been different, and all three now have something definite to show for them.

The uncertainty is considerable elsewhere. Mossdeep receives Sunyshore with the Hoenn–Sinnoh bye available. Mt. Silver goes to Cinnabar needing both a win and help from Saffron to secure the Kanto–Johto bye. Lavender can qualify by winning at Cerulean, just as an eight-week injury report removes Mr. Clanky from its available options. A favorable position does not spare a staff the next difficult assignment.
Seven clubs have qualified; five have division titles

body.text: Saffron’s division was settled when Vermilion lost 19–0 at Olivine. The Volts and Cerulean are both 7–7, leaving either with a maximum of ten victories against Saffron’s eleven. Cinnabar’s 31–19 victory, combined with Pewter’s loss at Mahogany, produces the same certainty in Kanto West: the Blaze have nine wins and the Rockers can reach only eight.

Petalburg’s guarantee requires the whole remaining schedule. Even if the Pride lose their last three games and receive the unfavorable side of every equal-record comparison, the conference cannot produce enough qualifying rivals to exclude them. That secures a berth; Rustboro and Dewford can still take Hoenn West. Their two remaining meetings with one another and Petalburg are particularly consequential now.

Seven teams qualify from each conference: four division winners followed by three wild cards. Division winners receive seeds one through four. Only the first seed rests during the opening round. X means a secured berth, Y a secured division, and Z the secured first seed and bye. Neither conference has a Z after Week 15.
Mossdeep can settle the bye against the only remaining challenger

Mossdeep needs a win or a tie at home against Sunyshore. A victory puts the Eclipse on fifteen wins, beyond every conference rival’s ceiling. A tie leaves Mossdeep with fourteen wins and a tie while Sunyshore can finish no better than thirteen wins and a tie. Petalburg can reach only thirteen wins. The calculation ends there.

A Sunyshore victory keeps the race open. If the Starseekers then beat Pastoria and Veilstone while Mossdeep loses to Sootopolis and Lavaridge, both finish 14–3. Sunyshore would hold the head-to-head win and take the first seed. Those results are a possible route, not a forecast of an Eclipse collapse. They explain exactly why an undefeated team still has something to clinch.

In that favorable combination, Eterna could still finish 9–8 while Canalave wins its last two to reach 9–8. The Bulwark could then have the superior division record after their split head-to-head series. The Thorns must keep attending to the remaining games against Oreburgh and Snowpoint.

Lavender’s win-and-in route depends on a tiebreak already protected against Violet. The Wails won their first meeting and have three division victories. Violet can finish with only two. Even if the Falcons win the rematch and match Lavender’s final overall record, they cannot take the higher division position. A tenth Lavender win therefore secures entry without another result. Olivine and Vermilion win their next two games to enter Week 18 at 9–7. Cerulean beats Lavender and loses to Saffron, arriving at 8–8. body.text: If Vermilion and Olivine both win, Lavender, the Volts, the Ironclads and Violet all finish 10–7. Violet misses. The division procedure first puts Lavender ahead of the Falcons; the wild-card procedure then awards each remaining place. Equal overall records give Violet a tiebreak hearing, not an automatic invitation.

If Vermilion wins while Olivine ties or loses, Violet qualifies with Lavender and Vermilion. If Vermilion ties while Olivine wins, the three become Lavender, Violet and Olivine. When both finales end tied, Olivine takes the last berth ahead of Vermilion at 9–7–1 on their head-to-head result: the 19–0 game just played. That result has acquired a clear use in a later argument.

Cerulean wins its finale and still misses in all three branches of this particular setup. Even if Olivine loses too, the Tide, Volts and Ironclads are 9–8 behind Lavender and Violet. Vermilion has the better division record than Cerulean; Olivine then wins the head-to-head comparison with Vermilion. Every named qualifying trio survives the later strength-of-victory and scoring tiebreaks. The chart does not promise exact seed order.
The current bracket is a starting position

If the present seed order held, Blackthorn would host Vermilion, Saffron would host Olivine, and Cinnabar would host Lavender. In Hoenn–Sinnoh, Sunyshore would host Mauville, Petalburg would host Dewford, and Eterna would host Rustboro. Mossdeep and Mt. Silver currently occupy the bye positions. Those are current pairings, not booked playoff games; the next three rounds can change both entry and placement.

Canalave at Rustboro is especially useful to follow alongside the marquee games. The Stone are 8–6 after losing 41–7 at Sunyshore, the Bulwark 7–7 after losing 51–7 to Mossdeep. Both have immediate reason to recover, and their result can also decide whether Petalburg celebrates a division title. Dewford hosts Oreburgh after its overtime loss at Hearthome. Mauville, now the seventh seed at 7–7, hosts Snowpoint before visiting Dewford and Petalburg. Those last two division games give the Dynamos direct opportunities to change the order above them.

body.text: Sunyshore visits unbeaten Mossdeep with the Hoenn–Sinnoh bye at stake. Mt. Silver takes its changed quarterback situation to newly crowned Kanto West champion Cinnabar, and Blackthorn visits Saffron in a meeting of eleven-win teams. Lavender can clinch a berth at Cerulean. Everyone plays again: sixteen matchups, with five separate judgments and scorelines for each.

I went 11–5 last week, though Sunyshore made my 30–20 pick look needlessly cautious by beating Rustboro 41–7. The Starseekers met my target of holding the Stone below twenty-four, but neither side lost a turnover, so the requested turnover-margin win never arrived. Rustboro missed its target of three completions gaining at least twenty yards. Mossdeep met both of my targets at Canalave: two conversions in four third downs and fewer than fourteen points allowed. This week the Eclipse face a much more productive offense. My pick is Mossdeep 38, Sunyshore 21; the full Game of the Week preview explains why.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Bibarel ran for one hundred yards and two touchdowns against Fuchsia. Viridian has scored nine points in its last two games; I expect Cianwood's limited but useful ground attack to provide enough separation.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Viridian followed fifty-six points allowed with only three points scored. Cianwood does not need an ambitious passing afternoon to beat that combination; Bibarel can keep the visitors ahead of the difficult downs.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Crushers remain without Gardevoir and two receivers. Their run game offers a way through, but ninety-five passing yards against Fuchsia leave little insurance if Viridian begins tackling Bibarel before the second level.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Cianwood has won two straight after losing to Lavender by one. That steadier stretch carries more weight for me than Viridian's home field, though the Crushers' passing absences should keep this modest.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Titans have 162 points in fourteen games and just managed ninety passing yards against Violet. Give Cianwood another afternoon of productive Bibarel carries and Viridian will need an offensive transformation to answer.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Iron Jugulis threw for 286 yards against Viridian, while Fuchsia's Empoleon finished with eighty-two and two interceptions at Cianwood. Violet has the stronger recent passing evidence and faces a defense missing Kleavor.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Fuchsia has scored seven in each of its last two games. Violet finally stopped losing, and a defense allowing 301 points offers enough room for Iron Jugulis to make the recovery look convincing.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Violet needed 286 passing yards to score seventeen. I like the Falcons' advantage against Fuchsia's injured secondary, but finishing drives remains a separate job from accumulating completions.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Falcons' defense just held Viridian to three, which should make the next trip less anxious. Fuchsia can compete at home, but the visitors have more ways to recover from an ordinary stalled possession.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Empoleon threw two interceptions while Fuchsia generated eighty-two passing yards. Violet can turn those empty possessions into a decisive lead; this is a matchup where picking a narrow escape would require more optimism about the home offense than I possess.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Pewter managed thirty-eight passing yards at Mahogany. Olivine's receiver injuries limit its own ceiling, but a defense fresh from shutting out Vermilion should give Drampa enough possessions to find two touchdowns.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: The Rockers have scored three, seventeen and nine in their last three games. Olivine already found a way to win nineteen-zero with an injured receiving group; Pewter offers another manageable offensive assignment.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Olivine intercepted the chance for a recovery against Vermilion, but its offense still threw a pick and missed chances around two touchdowns. Pewter's Delcatty and Cranidos combined for 105 rushing yards at Mahogany; that can keep a home upset within reach.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I expect a slow game between offenses that have earned caution. Olivine's latest defensive performance gives it a slight advantage, with Magmar's six catches providing Drampa a useful outlet despite the absent receivers.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Pewter's passing game produced thirty-eight yards last week. Olivine can afford to be patient against that, and I expect the Ironclads to make Brock explain another afternoon in which three points feel like a major event.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Vermilion has scored nine points across three losses. Mahogany just won with two rushing touchdowns and 201 passing yards; even with its tight-end injuries, the Frost have shown the more credible route to sustained offense.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: The Volts have been shut out twice in three weeks, most recently by a seven-win Olivine club. Mahogany needs only ordinary work from Porygon-Z to make the home team's next scoring drought costly.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Mahogany's missing tight ends and guard Quilladin keep me from expecting easy movement. Vermilion still has to prove it can turn Chandelure's completions into touchdown opportunities, and the recent record favors the Frost narrowly.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Mahogany has a difficult injury list and is leaving home after a welcome win. I expect Vermilion to find enough improvement against this opponent to end the skid, with its defense keeping the required score low.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Three weeks have produced nine Vermilion points. Mahogany scored seventeen while its passing and running games both contributed against Pewter; I will trust that evidence before promising a Volts revival because the calendar changed.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Crem Ftzpatrik supplied a touchdown and the winning drive against Saffron after Tic Thorpe's injury. Cinnabar's four-touchdown passing response at Blackthorn makes this dangerous, but Mt. Silver's receivers and season-long defense earn a narrow road pick.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Tic Thorpe is out six weeks, and the Reds allowed nine sacks before escaping Saffron. Gholdengo just threw for 323 yards against Blackthorn; I like Cinnabar's settled passing attack at home against a visitor reorganizing its most important position.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Garshawn Lynch gave Mt. Silver seventy-six rushing yards and seventy-four receiving yards against Saffron. That dual outlet can reduce what Ftzpatrik must solve, while Cinnabar's new Seismitoad absence removes one of its backfield options.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Ftzpatrik handled the final possession well, but a full road game brings a longer examination. Cinnabar has Arcanine coming off 138 receiving yards and Gholdengo playing confidently; I expect the home passing game to supply one more finish.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Reds beat Saffron while their quarterback situation changed and their kicker scored eighteen points. Gregar Jenings still caught 138 yards. I trust Mt. Silver to build a workable plan around those remaining strengths and remind Cinnabar that a division title does not make this defense ordinary.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Saffron recorded nine sacks at Mt. Silver and now faces a Blackthorn offense that lost two fumbles against Cinnabar. With Archam Manning coming off 299 yards and no interceptions, I favor the Psi Corps turning pressure into a cleaner home win.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: NeMarcus Tare collected seven sacks against the conference leader. Blackthorn just allowed thirty-one at home, and Saffron has the passing and rushing production to make another shaky Dragons afternoon expensive.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Saffron's three lost fumbles explain why its rush did not finish the job at Mt. Silver. I expect better ball security at home, with Dam Skattebo's rushing threat keeping Blackthorn from concentrating every answer on Manning.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Both clubs are eleven-three, and Blackthorn still has Hatterene completing twenty-five of thirty-three last week. Saffron's pressure and home field give it my edge, but I expect a closer game than the Dragons' latest defensive result suggests.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Saffron scored thirty-three despite three lost fumbles. Blackthorn allowed four touchdown passes to Gholdengo and still lacks Grovyle; the Psi Corps can punish both sides of that matchup before another late rally becomes necessary.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Azalea's Drampa threw two touchdowns without an interception, while Celadon rallied within three of Lavender with Infernape. The Bloom have allowed thirty-three fewer season points and get this matchup at home; I favor them narrowly.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Azalea moved the ball for 298 yards against Cerulean and got eighty-two receiving yards from Vivillon. Celadon's missing safety Frosmoth makes that passing improvement more interesting than the Bloom's late cosmetic recovery at Lavender.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Celadon forced a punt-return fumble and built two late touchdown drives against Lavender. Azalea's seventeen points came with another loss; I favor the Bloom sustaining their recent passing progress through more of the game.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Infernape's difficult afternoon ended with a useful scoring drive, and Celadon has played several competitive games lately. The Bloom's quarterback absence remains significant, but their recent defense gives them room to survive another close finish.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Celadon scored thirty-four against Cerulean and held Pewter to three before its narrow Lavender loss. Azalea has twenty points in two games. I expect the Bloom's home offense to establish a lead that the visitors cannot match possession for possession.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Frosmoth threw 163 yards and a touchdown in relief of the now-injured Mr. Clanky. Lavender has won five straight and can clinch with a win; I trust its defense to make a modest passing afternoon sufficient against Cerulean.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cerulean has won three straight, including its one-point result against Cinnabar. Lavender loses Mr. Clanky for eight weeks and still lacks People Eater; the Tide can make those missing options matter more than the Wails' recent record.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Might Guy caught both Lavender touchdown passes, one from each quarterback, against Celadon. Frosmoth has an established productive target, and the Wails' defense can keep Cerulean from turning this into a broad passing contest.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Lavender has kept finding useful answers as its available players change. Cerulean's own three-win run deserves respect, but I expect Frosmoth and Might Guy to provide enough continuity for the Wails to earn the clinching result.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Wails are nine-five with a minus-forty-five scoring margin, and their newest quarterback injury removes 121 yards of last week's passing production. Cerulean has won three consecutive close games; I expect its receivers to make this the least comfortable stop in Lavender's recent run.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mauville scored twenty-nine at Veilstone with Togekiss throwing three touchdowns. Snowpoint moved the ball against Sootopolis but lost two fumbles and never reached the end zone; I favor the Dynamos finishing more possessions at home.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Snowpoint has fifteen points across its last two games. Mauville finally found a passing score beyond the low teens, and a home matchup against another struggling offense gives that improvement a useful chance to last.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Snowpoint gained 298 yards against Sootopolis and did not punt. Its problem was finishing and ball security, both more repairable than an offense unable to move at all; I expect a cleaner game to expose Mauville's still modest season production.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Dynamos have won consecutive close games, one in overtime. I expect another uneven afternoon, but their home passing options should produce the extra touchdown that Snowpoint has struggled to find.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Snowpoint turned sixty plays into nine points last week. Mauville has a receiver in Tangrowth coming off seven catches and a touchdown, and I expect that simpler scoring connection to make the visitors' long possessions feel increasingly unhelpful.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Vigoroth rushed for eighty-seven yards and a touchdown against Mauville. Sootopolis escaped Snowpoint despite being outgained and has allowed 292 season points; I expect Veilstone to sustain enough drives to win a close road game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Sootopolis has won two of three, while Veilstone needed overtime only to lose its last game. Drampa threw for 186 yards without an interception at Snowpoint; I favor the steadier home quarterback against a five-win visitor.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Surge allowed Snowpoint to run sixty plays without punting. Veilstone's Vigoroth can turn that kind of sustained possession into touchdowns, and I expect its balanced work to be more productive than last week's turnover-heavy visitor.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Sootopolis keeps finding narrow wins around a defense that gives it anxious stretches. Veilstone's rushing game should keep this competitive, but the Surge's recent ability to finish a low-scoring afternoon earns my home pick.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Veilstone has scored 151 points in fourteen games. Sootopolis gets a chance to make its passing game the larger part of the afternoon, and I expect the home receivers to exploit a defense that just surrendered twenty-nine to Mauville.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Excadrill ran for ninety-four yards at Hearthome even as Dewford's passing game stalled. Oreburgh has allowed 271 points and just lost at home to Fortree; the Breakers can build the more dependable scoring day around their runner.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Dewford needs a response after overtime, and Oreburgh brings three wins and a defense that allowed Rabsca three touchdown passes. The Breakers should be able to support Excadrill with more passing production than last week's 102 yards.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Oreburgh allowed twenty-four despite a competitive rushing and receiving effort of its own. Dewford's healthy offense has a clear way to keep the Miners defending repeated runs, then punish the shorter passing opportunities those possessions create.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Oreburgh has lost several close games and scored twenty-one against Fortree. I expect the Miners to stay involved again, but Dewford's ground game and home field give it the better closing possession.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Breakers have eight wins; the Miners have three and just made Fortree look comfortable throwing touchdowns. I expect Dewford to stop asking a one-touchdown passing day to do enough and give Excadrill a much more useful cushion.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Hearthome has allowed nineteen points across two wins since Sunyshore's visit. Fortree is throwing more productively but still carries 362 points allowed; I favor the Haunts' improving defense to separate two capable recent passing efforts.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Rabsca followed 230 passing yards against Rustboro with three touchdown passes at Oreburgh. Fortree's offense is improving while Hearthome leaves home after two wins; I expect the Skyhawks to keep the better part of their recovery going.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Fortree has scored twenty-three and twenty-four since the Mossdeep defeat, but its missing Pawmot and Banette weaken the defensive choices. Hearthome just produced 245 passing yards against Dewford and can test that depth.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Hearthome has answered a fifty-three-point defeat with two useful wins. I trust that defensive response to travel better than Fortree's latest narrow escape, while allowing that Rabsca has made the home offense more credible.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Fortree has surrendered 362 points, and two improved offensive afternoons do not reduce that total. Hearthome's Frosmoth found several productive receivers against Dewford; I expect the Haunts to keep making the Skyhawks defend the entire passing possession.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Eterna has scored sixteen points in two losses, while Petalburg recovered from Mossdeep with three touchdowns at Pastoria. The Thorns' defense should keep this close, but I favor the Pride's healthier recent passing finish at home.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Petalburg has ten wins and just found twenty-one points against Pastoria's disruptive defense. Eterna could not reach fourteen against Lavaridge; I expect the Pride to protect their division opportunity with the more reliable finishing offense.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Eterna's season defense has allowed 157 points, ninety-eight fewer than Petalburg's. The Thorns can make Iron Valiant repeat difficult throws while Tatsugiri builds on 219 passing yards against Lavaridge; I favor a defensive road upset.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Both clubs have earned a position worth protecting through a series of narrow games. Petalburg's one-point win at Pastoria gives me slightly more confidence in its ability to complete the final useful possession at home.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Petalburg is ten-four and has still allowed more points than it has scored. Eterna's defense gives the Thorns an excellent chance to expose another low-output Pride afternoon without needing a suddenly spectacular offense.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Pastoria scored twenty against Petalburg after combining for thirteen in its previous two games. Oinkologne and Watchog supplied 107 rushing yards; I favor that broader attack narrowly over a Lavaridge team still allowing more than twenty-two points a game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Delphox threw three touchdowns at Eterna, whose defense has been substantially better than Pastoria's by season points allowed. Lavaridge can carry that passing confidence home and make the Waves chase a score again.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Pastoria has created difficult passing conditions recently, including seven sacks against Eterna. Lavaridge's passing improvement is real, but I expect the Waves' rush and two productive runners to make a more complete afternoon.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Pastoria lost by one after a much better offensive showing. Lavaridge also has a useful win to build on, but I think the Waves' steadier season defense will make a small score hold up this time.

picks.author: dorian-pike

picks.author: tessa-wren

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Rustboro's Gibby Timmy still produced a fifty-four-yard catch in the Sunyshore defeat. Canalave has been unable to make its own possessions pay for three weeks; I expect the Stone to find enough deep completions to leave that problem exposed.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Rustboro converted one of eleven third downs and ran for twenty-six yards at Sunyshore. Canalave gained 334 yards against Mossdeep, so I expect more resistance than its seven points suggest, with the Stone winning a narrow protection-and-finishing contest.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Both clubs have just met difficult opponents. Canalave's Seismitoad still rushed for eighty-one yards against Mossdeep, which gives the visitors a workable approach, but Rustboro's home receivers offer the better way to answer a late score.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Canalave has scored 135 points all season. Rustboro has almost twice that total and can recover against a much less explosive opponent than Sunyshore; I expect Tyler Scarboro to get several possessions worth discussing favorably.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Sunyshore brings 144 rushing yards from Myles Gabite and four receiving touchdowns from 88 Special against Rustboro. Mossdeep has scored 185 in three games, and Serp Gardener's continuing absence leaves the visitors short a coverage option against Dram Marino and Accel BeckhmJr.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Sunyshore just beat Rustboro more emphatically than Mossdeep did, and its running game can keep this competitive. I still favor the Eclipse because BeckhmJr has 1,875 receiving yards and the Starseekers enter without Serp Gardener.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Marino has fifty-four touchdown passes against three interceptions, and Mossdeep has scored seven passing touchdowns in each of its last two games. Sunyshore's good rush against Rustboro will face a passing offense far better equipped to punish an unsuccessful pressure.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Starseekers have scored 111 points across three wins and have several productive receivers around DeZhaun Watzon. I expect them to make Mossdeep work, with the unbeaten club's passing consistency supplying the final margin.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Myles Gabite ran for 144 yards while Sunyshore spread twenty-three completions among five receivers against Rustboro. That gives the Starseekers a way to sustain possessions and make Mossdeep answer a balanced contender; I am backing Karson Jones to finish the upset.
